items.name: The Executive Vesting Clause assigns federal executive power to one President, n
items.summary: The Executive Vesting Clause assigns federal executive power to one President, not to Congress or a collection of separate Presidents.

items.name: The original four-year terms of President and Vice President remain part of cons
items.summary: The original four-year terms of President and Vice President remain part of constitutional office tenure.

items.name: The Twentieth Amendment Section 1 sets presidential and vice-presidential terms
items.summary: The Twentieth Amendment Section 1 sets presidential and vice-presidential terms to end and successor terms to begin at noon on January 20.

items.name: The Twenty-Second Amendment generally limits election to the Presidency to twice
items.summary: The Twenty-Second Amendment generally limits election to the Presidency to twice and imposes a one-election limit after service as President or Acting President for more than two years of another's elected term, subject to historic transitional exceptions.
items.note: It limits elections, not a blanket textual cap on all possible service durations.

items.name: The executive vesting clause does not itself create authority to legislate, disp
items.summary: The executive vesting clause does not itself create authority to legislate, dispense with binding law, appropriate funds, or displace congressional enumerated powers.
items.note: Interpretive legal conclusions require controlling cases (Youngstown framework) and statutes; this record does not assert a judicial holding.

items.name: Presidential electors are appointed by each state in the manner directed by its
items.summary: Presidential electors are appointed by each state in the manner directed by its legislature, subject to the Constitution and valid election law.

items.name: Each state appoints presidential electors equal to its Senators plus Representat
items.summary: Each state appoints presidential electors equal to its Senators plus Representatives in Congress.

items.name: A Senator, Representative, or holder of federal office of trust or profit is ine
items.summary: A Senator, Representative, or holder of federal office of trust or profit is ineligible to serve as a presidential elector.

items.name: The Twenty-Third Amendment gives the District of Columbia presidential electors,
items.summary: The Twenty-Third Amendment gives the District of Columbia presidential electors, under congressional direction and a ceiling based on the least populous state.
items.note: DC electoral authority comes from Amendment XXIII rather than transforming DC into a State.

items.name: The Fourteenth Amendment Section 3 adds disqualification conditions for electors
items.summary: The Fourteenth Amendment Section 3 adds disqualification conditions for electors and specified offices, with scope and enforcement governed by controlling law.
items.note: ARFI does not determine contested disqualification facts or independently apply Section 3; precedent will be represented separately.

items.name: Original undifferentiated electoral votes and contingent-election procedures wer
items.summary: Original undifferentiated electoral votes and contingent-election procedures were superseded by the Twelfth Amendment.

items.name: The operative presidential and vice-presidential ballots, majority requirements
items.summary: The operative presidential and vice-presidential ballots, majority requirements and contingent election mechanisms are prescribed by the Twelfth Amendment, not the old Article II clause.
items.note: This points to current replacement law without treating a superseded norm as currently binding.

items.name: Congress may determine the time of choosing electors and the day on which they g
items.summary: Congress may determine the time of choosing electors and the day on which they give votes.

items.name: The presidential electors' day of voting must be the same throughout the United
items.summary: The presidential electors' day of voting must be the same throughout the United States.

items.name: Specific national election dates, certification deadlines and counting procedure
items.summary: Specific national election dates, certification deadlines and counting procedures depend on enacted law and amendments not specified in the original timing clause.

items.name: Presidential eligibility includes the original natural-born-citizen criterion, w
items.summary: Presidential eligibility includes the original natural-born-citizen criterion, without deciding contested definitions beyond the text.

items.name: The alternative citizenship-at-the-adoption-of-the-Constitution qualification is
items.summary: The alternative citizenship-at-the-adoption-of-the-Constitution qualification is a historical transition provision, not an additional currently satisfiable route to eligibility.
items.note: Historical portion of a still-operative eligibility clause; no original officeholder is now eligible through this founding-era exception.

items.name: Presidential eligibility requires at least thirty-five years of age.
items.summary: Presidential eligibility requires at least thirty-five years of age.

items.name: Presidential eligibility requires fourteen years of residence within the United
items.summary: Presidential eligibility requires fourteen years of residence within the United States.

items.name: The Twenty-Second Amendment adds an election limit distinct from original Articl
items.summary: The Twenty-Second Amendment adds an election limit distinct from original Article II age, citizenship and residence qualifications.

items.name: The Twelfth Amendment makes a person constitutionally ineligible for the Preside
items.summary: The Twelfth Amendment makes a person constitutionally ineligible for the Presidency ineligible for the Vice Presidency as well.

items.name: The Fourteenth Amendment Section 3 may add federal office disqualification condi
items.summary: The Fourteenth Amendment Section 3 may add federal office disqualification conditions to officeholding; application and enforcement require controlling precedent.
items.note: Not an automatic legal determination of a particular person's eligibility.

items.name: The Twenty-Fifth Amendment clarifies that on presidential removal, death or resi
items.summary: The Twenty-Fifth Amendment clarifies that on presidential removal, death or resignation, the Vice President becomes President.
items.note: Distinguish permanent succession from temporary inability (Acting President).

items.name: Under Amendment XXV Section 2, a vice-presidential vacancy is filled by presiden
items.summary: Under Amendment XXV Section 2, a vice-presidential vacancy is filled by presidential nomination and majority confirmation by both Houses of Congress.
items.note: Not the Senate advice-and-consent process used for executive appointments.

items.name: Under Amendment XXV Section 3, written presidential inability declaration to spe
items.summary: Under Amendment XXV Section 3, written presidential inability declaration to specified congressional presiding officers temporarily transfers powers to Vice President as Acting President until a contrary declaration.

items.name: Under Amendment XXV Section 4, the Vice President and a majority of specified pr
items.summary: Under Amendment XXV Section 4, the Vice President and a majority of specified principal executive officers (or authorized substitute body) may declare inability; contested restoration has additional deadlines and two-thirds voting requirements.
items.note: A distinct temporary inability route, not the original constitutional impeachment procedure.

items.name: Amendment XXV Section 4 prescribes 4-day, 48-hour assembly, and 21-day congressi
items.summary: Amendment XXV Section 4 prescribes 4-day, 48-hour assembly, and 21-day congressional decision periods under their respective triggering conditions.

items.name: Congress may provide by law for dual presidential/vice-presidential vacancies or
items.summary: Congress may provide by law for dual presidential/vice-presidential vacancies or inability, within later amendments and presidential succession law.

items.name: Amendment XX Section 3 governs death or failure of the President-elect to qualif
items.summary: Amendment XX Section 3 governs death or failure of the President-elect to qualify and corresponding Vice-President-elect transition and congressional contingency powers.

items.name: Presidential compensation must neither increase nor decrease during the term for
items.summary: Presidential compensation must neither increase nor decrease during the term for which the President was elected.

items.name: During that term, the President may not receive additional emoluments from the U
items.summary: During that term, the President may not receive additional emoluments from the United States or from any State.

items.name: The Foreign Emoluments Clause of Article I Section 9 Clause 8 is a separate prov
items.summary: The Foreign Emoluments Clause of Article I Section 9 Clause 8 is a separate provision with distinct covered persons and consent conditions.
items.note: Whether any particular President or transaction falls within foreign-emoluments doctrine requires legal review.

items.name: The prescribed oath or affirmation must be taken before the President enters on
items.summary: The prescribed oath or affirmation must be taken before the President enters on execution of the office.

items.name: The oath or affirmation expressly commits to faithful execution and to preserve,
items.summary: The oath or affirmation expressly commits to faithful execution and to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution to the best of the President's ability.

items.name: The oath neither creates independent legislative powers nor removes the Presiden
items.summary: The oath neither creates independent legislative powers nor removes the President's duty to execute constitutionally valid federal law.

items.name: The President is Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States.
items.summary: The President is Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States.

items.name: Constitutional Commander-in-Chief authority over state militia applies when the
items.summary: Constitutional Commander-in-Chief authority over state militia applies when the militia has been called into actual service of the United States.

items.name: Article I reserves declaring war, Army and Navy organization, military regulatio
items.summary: Article I reserves declaring war, Army and Navy organization, military regulation and funding powers to Congress; the Commander-in-Chief role does not alone displace them.
items.note: Actual conflict allocation and use of force under statutes and judicial doctrine deferred.

items.name: Article I §8 cl16 reserves to states appointment of militia officers and specifi
items.summary: Article I §8 cl16 reserves to states appointment of militia officers and specified training authority under federally prescribed discipline.

items.name: The President may require written opinions of principal officers of executive de
items.summary: The President may require written opinions of principal officers of executive departments on subjects relating to their respective duties.

items.name: The constitutional pardon and reprieve authority concerns offenses against the U
items.summary: The constitutional pardon and reprieve authority concerns offenses against the United States, not state-law offenses.

items.name: Presidential pardons and reprieves explicitly except cases of impeachment.
items.summary: Presidential pardons and reprieves explicitly except cases of impeachment.

items.name: Treaties require Senate advice and consent, with concurrence of two thirds of Se
items.summary: Treaties require Senate advice and consent, with concurrence of two thirds of Senators present.

items.name: Nomination and appointment of specified federal principal officers and Supreme C
items.summary: Nomination and appointment of specified federal principal officers and Supreme Court judges occur by President with Senate advice and consent.

items.name: The treaty-specific two-thirds Senate concurrence requirement must not be applie
items.summary: The treaty-specific two-thirds Senate concurrence requirement must not be applied to ordinary appointments as if the text also specified it for nominations.

items.name: Other officers of the United States covered by this appointments clause hold off
items.summary: Other officers of the United States covered by this appointments clause hold offices established by law, with constitutional exceptions for appointments elsewhere provided.

items.name: Congress may vest appointment of such inferior officers as it thinks proper in P
items.summary: Congress may vest appointment of such inferior officers as it thinks proper in President alone, courts of law, or heads of departments, but it must do so by law.

items.name: An Appointments Clause record does not create a modern agency, authorize every d
items.summary: An Appointments Clause record does not create a modern agency, authorize every delegated role, or eliminate statutory limits on the office.

items.name: Recess-appointment power is expressly associated with Senate recess vacancies an
items.summary: Recess-appointment power is expressly associated with Senate recess vacancies and temporary commissions; specifics of constitutional reach depend on precedent.

items.name: A commission issued as a recess appointment expires at the end of the Senate's n
items.summary: A commission issued as a recess appointment expires at the end of the Senate's next session.

items.name: The original text alone does not resolve what qualifies as a Senate recess or wh
items.summary: The original text alone does not resolve what qualifies as a Senate recess or when vacancies may happen for purposes of later controlling decisions.
items.note: NLRB v. Noel Canning and subsequent treatment belong in the future doctrine register.

items.name: The President must provide Congress information on the state of the Union from t
items.summary: The President must provide Congress information on the state of the Union from time to time.

items.name: The President may recommend measures deemed necessary and expedient to Congress,
items.summary: The President may recommend measures deemed necessary and expedient to Congress, but does not enact federal legislation by recommendation alone.

items.name: The presidential power to convene both Houses or either one is expressly limited
items.summary: The presidential power to convene both Houses or either one is expressly limited to extraordinary occasions.

items.name: Presidential adjournment under Article II §3 depends on disagreement between the
items.summary: Presidential adjournment under Article II §3 depends on disagreement between the Houses over the time of adjournment.

items.name: The President's exceptional adjournment authority concerns the time of adjournme
items.summary: The President's exceptional adjournment authority concerns the time of adjournment; it does not permit dissolving Congress or indefinite suspension.

items.name: The President is directed to receive ambassadors and other public ministers.
items.summary: The President is directed to receive ambassadors and other public ministers.

items.name: The textual reception duty must not be treated as a full verbatim grant of every
items.summary: The textual reception duty must not be treated as a full verbatim grant of every recognized foreign-relations prerogative.
items.note: Judicial recognition doctrine (including Zivotofsky) will be mapped as secondary judicial holdings, not original text.

items.name: The President shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
items.summary: The President shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed.

items.name: The Take Care duty does not itself permit Treasury withdrawals absent appropriat
items.summary: The Take Care duty does not itself permit Treasury withdrawals absent appropriations made by law.

items.name: Whether particular disputed statutes or executive actions comply with the Consti
items.summary: Whether particular disputed statutes or executive actions comply with the Constitution requires a distinct statute and judicial doctrine analysis.
items.note: Do not treat an ARFI summary as authorizing selective noncompliance or executive lawmaking.

items.name: The President must commission all officers of the United States.
items.summary: The President must commission all officers of the United States.

items.name: The duty to commission officers is separate from the constitutional nomination,
items.summary: The duty to commission officers is separate from the constitutional nomination, appointment and Senate-consent mechanisms.

items.name: The impeachment/removal provision reaches the President, Vice President and civi
items.summary: The impeachment/removal provision reaches the President, Vice President and civil Officers of the United States.

items.name: Removal by impeachment and conviction is based on treason, bribery, or other hig
items.summary: Removal by impeachment and conviction is based on treason, bribery, or other high crimes and misdemeanors.

items.name: The House alone has the power of impeachment under Article I §2 cl5.
items.summary: The House alone has the power of impeachment under Article I §2 cl5.

items.name: Conviction on impeachment requires two thirds of Senators present, sitting under
items.summary: Conviction on impeachment requires two thirds of Senators present, sitting under oath; the Chief Justice presides in a presidential trial.

items.name: Constitutional removal occurs upon impeachment and conviction; impeachment by th
items.summary: Constitutional removal occurs upon impeachment and conviction; impeachment by the House alone is not itself Senate conviction.

items.name: Article II §2 cl1 excludes cases of impeachment from presidential pardon power.
items.summary: Article II §2 cl1 excludes cases of impeachment from presidential pardon power.

items.name: Article I §3 cl7 separates limited impeachment judgment from potential indictmen
items.summary: Article I §3 cl7 separates limited impeachment judgment from potential indictment, trial and punishment according to law.

items.name: Determinations about covered civil officers, high crimes and misdemeanors, trial
items.summary: Determinations about covered civil officers, high crimes and misdemeanors, trial jurisdiction and disqualification follow authoritative constitutional interpretation and history, not this summary.
